group.title: People and places
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: A person whose job is to help others learn.
examples: Our {teacher} explains every new word.
wrong: A teacher is a place where we buy bread.

words.meaning: A person who treats people who are ill.
examples: I went to the {doctor} because I had a fever.
wrong: The doctor fixes cars in a garage.

words.meaning: A person who studies at a school or college.
examples: Every {student} gets a new book.
wrong: A student is someone who teaches the class.

words.meaning: A woman who has a child.
examples: My {mother} makes soup on Sundays.
wrong: My mother is the son of my grandmother.

words.meaning: A man who has a child.
examples: My {father} drives me to school.
wrong: My father is my brother’s sister.

words.meaning: A girl or woman who has the same parents as you.
examples: My {sister} is two years older than me.
wrong: My sister is a boy in my family.

words.meaning: A boy or man who has the same parents as you.
examples: My {brother} plays football every weekend.
wrong: My brother is the daughter of my mother.

words.meaning: A very young child.
examples: The {baby} sleeps for most of the day.
wrong: The baby runs a long race every morning.

words.meaning: An adult male person.
examples: The {man} on the bus gave me his seat.
wrong: A man is a young girl.

words.meaning: An adult female person.
examples: That {woman} is my English teacher.
wrong: A woman is a boy of ten.

words.meaning: A young person who is not yet an adult.
examples: Each {child} gets a small gift.
wrong: A child is a person over ninety.

words.meaning: A group of people who are related, such as parents and children.
examples: My {family} has dinner together every night.
wrong: A family is a kind of fruit.

words.meaning: The word or words that people call you.
examples: Please write your {name} here.
wrong: A name is a place where you sleep.

words.meaning: The work that a person does to earn money.
examples: She has a new {job} at a hotel.
wrong: A job is something you eat for breakfast.

words.meaning: A building where people live.
examples: They bought a small {house} near the river.
wrong: A house is a kind of animal.

words.meaning: A place where children go to learn.
examples: My brother walks to {school} every day.
wrong: A school is a place where we buy shoes.

words.meaning: A place where you buy things.
examples: The {shop} on the corner sells fresh bread.
wrong: A shop is a place where we sleep at night.

words.meaning: A large and important town.
examples: Tokyo is a very big {city}.
wrong: A city is a very small farm.

words.meaning: A green place in a town where people can walk and play.
examples: We play football in the {park} on Sundays.
wrong: A park is a room for cooking.

words.meaning: A place where doctors and nurses care for sick people.
examples: My aunt works at the {hospital}.
wrong: A hospital is a place where we buy toys.

words.meaning: A place where trains or buses stop.
examples: The train leaves from the {station} at nine.
wrong: A station is a kind of drink.

words.meaning: A place where you can buy and eat a meal.
examples: We had dinner at a small {restaurant}.
wrong: A restaurant is a place where we wash clothes.

words.meaning: A piece of land near a house with flowers or vegetables.
examples: There are red flowers in the {garden}.
wrong: A garden is a machine that cooks food.

words.meaning: A long stream of water that flows to the sea.
examples: The {river} runs through the middle of the town.
wrong: A river is a very tall building.

words.meaning: A very high hill.
examples: They climbed the {mountain} in two days.
wrong: A mountain is a small flat field.

words.meaning: A sandy place next to the sea.
examples: The children built a castle on the {beach}.
wrong: A beach is a place full of snow and no water.

words.meaning: An area of land with its own government, such as Japan.
examples: Brazil is a big {country}.
wrong: A country is a kind of sandwich.

words.meaning: A drawing that shows where places are.
examples: Look at the {map} to find the museum.
wrong: A map is a person who drives the bus.

words.meaning: A road vehicle with four wheels and an engine.
examples: My uncle drives a small red {car}.
wrong: A car is an animal that lives in a river.

words.meaning: A large vehicle that carries many people along a road.
examples: I take the {bus} to school.
wrong: A bus is a thing you wear on your head.

words.meaning: A long vehicle that runs on rails and carries people.
examples: The {train} to Boston leaves at noon.
wrong: A train is a kind of hat.

words.meaning: A vehicle with two wheels that you move with your feet.
examples: She rides her {bicycle} to the park.
wrong: A bicycle is a vehicle with four engines and a roof.

words.meaning: A place where planes land and take off.
examples: We arrived at the {airport} two hours early.
wrong: An airport is a place where we sleep in a tent.

words.meaning: A building where people pay to stay for a short time.
examples: We stayed in a small {hotel} near the beach.
wrong: A hotel is a place where we buy shoes.

words.meaning: Land and buildings where people grow food or keep animals.
examples: My grandfather has a {farm} with cows and chickens.
wrong: A farm is a city with many tall towers.

words.meaning: A piece of land with water all around it.
examples: We took a boat to a small {island}.
wrong: An island is land with no water anywhere near it.

words.meaning: A place that keeps people’s money.
examples: I put my money in the {bank}.
wrong: A bank is a place where we cook dinner.

words.meaning: A building where people can see old or important things.
examples: We saw old coins at the {museum}.
wrong: A museum is a place where we buy fresh fish.

words.meaning: A building where you can watch plays or films.
examples: We watched a funny film at the {theater}.
wrong: A theater is a place where we sleep at night.

words.meaning: A large area covered with trees.
examples: Many birds live in the {forest}.
wrong: A forest is a large city with no trees.
